lastCompletedGameRecap.recapHeadline: Deshaun Watson throws for 312 yards against his old team as the Browns rally past the Texans 27-24
lastCompletedGameRecap.recapLeadExcerpt: CLEVELAND -- — Deshaun Watson can talk all he wants about how playing the Houston Texans is just another game.  His coach doesn’t quite believe him.  Not after Watson's latest bit of last-minute thievery lifted the Cleveland Browns to a thrilling 27-24 win over the Texans on Sunday.  “I don’t care what he says,” coach Todd Monken.

injuryReport.name: Patrick Johnson
factors: Coaching/beat report confirms player will not be activated from IR this week
injuryReport.beatComment: Johnson was a full participant in Wednesday's practice in what was his first on-field action since being placed on injured reserve in late October due to a neck injury. His ability to practice in full is an encouraging sign, but Johnson would need to be activated from injured reserve in order to be available for Sunday's game against the Browns.

injuryReport.name: Adam Butler
factors: Remains in early stages of NFL 5-Step Concussion Protocol
injuryReport.beatComment: Butler enterted the NFL's concussion protocol after being ruled out for the remainder of the Raiders' Week 11 loss to the Broncos. The defensive tackle will need to be cleared by an independent neurologist to return to full-contact practice.

injuryReport.name: Tim Keenan III
injuryReport.beatComment: Keenan went down with a knee injury in the first half, and he will now officially be sidelined for the rest of Week 11. With Adam Butler (concussion) also done for the day, JJ Pegues will handle the bulk of the workload at defensive tackle versus the Broncos.

injuryReport.name: Tonka Hemingway
factors: Wednesday Limited Participation (LP); player toughness prior = 81%
injuryReport.beatComment: Hemingway did not play in the Raiders' Week 11 loss to the Broncos due to a stinger injury. The defensive lineman has continued to suffer the stinger's effects in Week 12 prep but has upgraded to a limited participant. Hemingway will likely need to upgrade to a full participant by Friday's practice for a chance to avoid any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Browns.

injuryReport.name: Brock Bowers
factors: Wednesday Limited Participation (LP); player toughness prior = 90%
injuryReport.beatComment: Bowers was sidelined for this past Sunday's 38-24 loss to the Broncos, but he's now practiced in a limited fashion in each of the Raiders' last three sessions. Though the Raiders have a bye looming in Week 13 that would give Bowers more time to recover from his lower-body injuries, Kubiak indicated that the break in the schedule won't be a factor in Bowers' status for this Sunday's matchup with the Browns, per Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com. Still, Bowers may need to advance to full practice participation by Friday in order to gain clearance for the Week 12 game.

injuryReport.name: JJ Pegues
injuryReport.beatComment: Pegues exited the Raiders' Week 11 loss to the Broncos late in the fourth quarter and did not return to the contest. The defensive tackle's full participation and injury clearance in the first prep session of Week 12 imply Pegues did not return to the Week 11 loss because he exited late, when the game was out of reach.

injuryReport.name: Dareke Young
injuryReport.beatComment: Young was diagnosed with a stinger in the first half of the Raiders' 38-24 loss to the Broncos and did not return. However, his ability to practice in full Wednesday indicates that the fifth-year wide receiver will be available for Sunday's road game against the Browns. Young has mostly operated on special teams this season and has not been targeted in the passing game since Week 4 against the Chiefs.

injuryReport.name: Michael Mayer
injuryReport.beatComment: Mayer missed out on a prime opportunity with top TE Brock Bowers (ankle/quadriceps) inactive in Week 11. When Bowers was out in Weeks 1 and 2 as he recovered from a meniscus trim in his left knee, Mayer went for a combined 9-55-0 line on 11 targets in those contests, but the latter also missed a stretch in the fourth quarter this Sunday due to a back injury. Bowers' status will be worth monitoring this week, as an absence from him next Sunday in Cleveland will set up Mayer for another key chance to produce.

coachingMatchup.headline: Todd Monken & DC Mike Rutenberg vs. HC Klint Kubiak, OC Andrew Janocko & DC Rob Leonard (Huntington Bank Field)
coachingMatchup.summary: Week 12 two-sided coordinator chess match pitting Cleveland Browns's staff (Todd Monken, OC Travis Switzer, DC Mike Rutenberg) against Las Vegas Raiders (4-7)—testing both Cleveland's offensive efficiency and its defensive pass-rush and coverage discipline.
bullets: Pass-Game Efficiency & Coverage Shell Delta: Todd Monken and OC Travis Switzer pair condensed splits with pre-snap jet motion and orbit motion to stress Las Vegas Raiders's single-high vs. two-high rotations—widening curl/flat defenders to attack the honey-hole between hook/curl linebackers and deep safeties on play-action choice/dagger concepts.

Trench Run-Fit & Two-Way Leverage: Against Las Vegas Raiders's pin-and-pull, counter, and duo runs targeting the A- and B-gaps, DC Mike Rutenberg balances four-man pressure with disguised Quarters and Cover 6 split-safety rotations on early downs and in the red zone.

Money-Down & Red-Zone Execution: Third-down conversion discipline and red-zone touchdown rate govern whether Cleveland sustains multi-play scoring drives or yields momentum to Las Vegas Raiders's pass rush and coverage disguises.
Tempo, Turnovers & Venue Leverage: Huntington Bank Field situational play-calling, penalty margin, and turnover differential provide the clearest late-game swing factors for both coaching staffs.

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Deshaun Watson, Harold Fannin Jr. & Denzel Boston vs. CB Eric Stokes & LB Nakobe Dean
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: CLE: #18 Pass Off (217.4 yds) · #24 Off. Scoring (-2.60) | LV: #29 Pass Def (+5.32)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Deshaun Watson, Harold Fannin Jr. & Denzel Boston attack the intermediate seams and middle-of-the-field leverage windows against Las Vegas Raiders's #29 pass defense (+5.32). Winning early-down timing throws keeps Cleveland's offense ahead of the chains and punishes disguised single-high rotations.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Watch Deshaun Watson (#4) scanning Raiders's deep safeties at the snap—when LB Nakobe Dean widens to take away the crossers, the intermediate seam opens immediately for Harold Fannin Jr. (#44).

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Jared Verse, Maliek Collins & Mason Graham vs. QB Fernando Mendoza & OT Kolton Miller
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: CLE: #16 Def Sacks (2.3/gm) | LV: #16 Pass Protection (6.5%)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Jared Verse, Maliek Collins & Mason Graham lead Cleveland's #16 NFL pass rush (2.3/gm) against Las Vegas Raiders's #16 pass-protection unit (6.5%). Collapsing the interior pocket without sending extra blitzers lets Browns keep seven defenders in coverage.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: On 3rd-and-6+, watch whether Jared Verse (#8) draw chip help from Raiders's tight ends or backs—creating 1-on-1 rush lanes inside for Maliek Collins (#96).

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Carson Schwesinger, Denzel Ward & Ronnie Hickman vs. WR Tre Tucker & QB Fernando Mendoza
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: CLE: #13 Pass Def (-0.19) | LV: #10 Pass Off (242.0 yds)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Carson Schwesinger, Denzel Ward & Ronnie Hickman anchor Cleveland's #13 pass defense (-0.19) against WR Tre Tucker and Las Vegas Raiders's #10 passing attack (242.0 yds). Limiting explosive 20+ yard chunk plays forces Raiders into sustained red-zone drives.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Track Carson Schwesinger (#49) at the top of routes against WR Tre Tucker: press-bail alignment with safety help over the top takes away QB Fernando Mendoza's preferred isolation shots.

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Quinshon Judkins & KC Concepcion vs. Raiders Front Seven & LB Nakobe Dean
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: CLE: #24 Rush Off (97.5 yds) | LV: #30 Rush Def (+0.90)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Quinshon Judkins & KC Concepcion test Las Vegas Raiders's #30 run defense (+0.90) with horizontal stretch and interior cutback lanes. Generating 4.5+ yards on first down unlocks play-action explosives and neutralizes Raiders's pass-rush packages.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Watch whether Raiders's linebackers over-pursue motion to the perimeter—opening decisive backside B-gap cutback lanes for Quinshon Judkins (#10).

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Spencer Fano, Zion Johnson & Elgton Jenkins vs. DT Folorunso Fatukasi & Raiders Simulated Pressures
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: CLE: #16 Pass Protection (6.0%) | LV: #16 Def Sacks (2.4/gm)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Spencer Fano, Zion Johnson & Elgton Jenkins protect Deshaun Watson (#16 protection at 6.0%) against DT Folorunso Fatukasi and Las Vegas Raiders's #16 pass rush (2.4/gm). Passing off interior twists and simulated blitzes cleanly determines late-down conversion efficiency.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Watch Spencer Fano (#55) on obvious passing downs—if DT Folorunso Fatukasi cannot win clean around the arc, Raiders must dial up interior stunts that stress Zion Johnson (#77).
